Casiphia
kuh-SIF-ee-uh
proper noun
Hebrew Kasiphya, a place of the Babylonian dispersion, perhaps “place of silver”; whence Ezra summoned Levites and Nethinim for the house of God.

Biblical Definition

Casiphia was a place of the dispersion, and Scripture remembers it for one holy errand. When Ezra mustered the returning remnant by the river of Ahava and looked over the company, he found among them not one of the sons of Levi, and no house of God can be raised or served without those whom the LORD has set apart to minister. So he sent to Casiphia: “And I sent them with commandment unto Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia…that they should bring unto us ministers for the house of our God” (Ezr 8:17). Out of that far settlement came Levites and Nethinim, servants of the sanctuary, to take their appointed places in the worship of the returning church. Here is a pattern the church must never forget. A remnant on the way home is not equipped for worship until the LORD provides ministers for His house; the ordinances He has commanded require the officers He has ordained. Ezra would not go up short-handed, offering God a worship stripped of the servants Scripture requires, for the God who commands the house also commands who shall serve in it. This is the regulative principle in the wilderness of exile: the church gathers not what pleases her, but what her Lord appoints. Casiphia sent her Levites, and the house of God was served according to the pattern. So still the King of the church raises up ministers and sends them where His people need them.

Webster 1828 Definition

A settlement of the dispersion whence Ezra summoned Levites and Nethinim for the house of God (Ezr 8:17); a witness that the returning church must be furnished with the ministers the LORD appoints for His worship.

CASIPHIA, a place of the Babylonian dispersion.

Whence Ezra summoned ministers for the house of God (Ezr 8:17).

The returning remnant lacked the sons of Levi for the sanctuary.

Ezra sent to Iddo the chief, and Levites and Nethinim came up.

A witness that worship requires the officers the LORD ordains.

Key Scripture

Ezr 8:17 — "And I sent them with commandment unto Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia, and I told them what they should say unto Iddo, and to his brethren the Nethinims, at the place Casiphia, that they should bring unto us ministers for the house of our God."

Mal 1:11 — "For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts."

Psa 133:3 — "As the dew of Hermon, and as the dew that descended upon the mountains of Zion: for there the LORD commanded the blessing, even life for evermore."

Modern Corruption

The dispersion settlement whence Ezra fetched Levites for the house of God; the entry recovers the truth that the LORD’s worship requires the ministers He ordains.

expand to see more

Casiphia is remembered for a single errand — the gathering of Levites for the return — and it raises no modern controversy. Its lesson is that the church on the way home must be furnished for worship according to God’s appointment.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that worship is regulated by the Lord who commands it, not shaped by the will of the worshipper. Ezra would not go up without the ministers Scripture required, for the God who ordains the house ordains who shall serve in it. So the King of the church still raises up and sends ministers, that His people may offer the pure offering His name deserves among the nations.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Kasiphya, a place-name of the dispersion, possibly connected with keseph, silver; a settlement of Levites in Babylon.

expand to see more

Casiphia — Hebrew Kasiphya, a place of the exile.

Perhaps linked to keseph, silver — a “place of silver.”

A settlement where Levites and Nethinim of the dispersion dwelt.

Iddo the chief was the man to whom Ezra sent (Ezr 8:17).

The Nethinim were the appointed servants of the sanctuary.

Usage

"Ezra sent to Casiphia for ministers for the house of God."

"The Levites of Casiphia came up with the returning remnant."

"Casiphia furnished the servants the sanctuary required."
